summary: Read all 809 entries of audit/vocabulary.txt (17,983 lines) and checked headword spelling and harakat, English meaning, gender, plural, listed forms, example sentences with their translations and the tap glosses. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: I found no misspelt headword, no wrong plural or gender, no agreement or case error in the example sentences, and no wrong English translation of a sentence. Almost every error is in the tap-gloss layer, which is clearly auto-filled from a shared dictionary: (1) person/gender mismatches between a verb form and its gloss (أَحَبَّ 'I', أَشْبَهَ 'I look like', سَبَحَتْ 'I swam', سَلَامَتُكِ 'to a man', خُطَّتُكَ 'to a woman', نَجَحْتُ 'you', and the recurring تَـ-verb glossed 'you (to a man)' where the subject is a woman or vice versa); (2) a verb form glossed as a different word altogether (شَعَرَ=hair, دَرَّسَ=lesson, حَجَزَ=booking, تَقَدَّمَ=progress, مَنَعَ=banning, تَخَرَّجَ=graduation, كُتَّاب=book, سَادَة=plain coffee, مُدَرِّسَة=school, شَرِيحَة=SIM card, الْإِشَارَة=pointing); (3) past 'he' forms glossed as imperatives (تَنَفَّسَ, كَرَّرَ, اِسْتَعْمَلَ, عَبَّرَ, خَمَّنَ, انْتَبَهَ); (4) two reviewer comments that leaked into learner-facing glosses and are wrong where they now sit (saih يَزُورُونَ, nashra الْأَخْبَارِ); (5) minor mood brackets ('after an', 'after lam') attached to plain indicative forms and senses copied from another sentence. 45 findings in all: 29 major (all gloss) and 16 minor, the minor ones being 11 gloss, 1 Arabic (sentence-initial hamzat waṣl left unvowelled in three places) and 4 engine (the four known quirks confirmed, and additionally رَأْي→Raʾī, مِائَة→Miāʾa, لِحًى→Liḥanā, أَسْهَلُ→ashalu, ة after ā → 'h'). 16 notes for the owner.
